Baby Q
CONTENTS
Housekeeping
DR SANDIE BOHIN (recalled)
Examination-in-chief by MR JOHNSON
Cross-examination by MR MYERS
Re-examination by MR JOHNSON
Summary of interview with LUCY LETBY re [Baby Q] (read)
MRS CLAIRE HOCKNELL (recalled)

Housekeeping
Mr Johnson, Mr Myers, before the jury come in, I've received some notes about sitting difficulties.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Of course one of the issues is that when the jury were empanelled the anticipated finish date was a little bit closer than it's likely to be.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Taking them in order, there is a request to have Friday, 21 April off. That's our first week back where we're starting with half a day on Monday, not sitting Tuesday, then Wednesday, Thursday, and then Friday would be off. That actually might not be an inconvenient day for the jury not to be here in fact.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes, there may be things to be dealt with.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: So I will say yes to that particular request.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Then we get to May. The 22nd, 23rd and 26th, which are Monday, Tuesday and Friday of that week. It is for a very good reason in fact because the juror in question put everything off to then, but that's the last possible date that can be accommodated, anticipating that the trial would have finished by then. So I'm
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: minded to set his mind at rest and say that we will not be sitting on those days.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes. I'm pretty sure that almost -- however things pan out, we will be able to make some use of at least some of that.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Exactly. So I'll deal with that now because we're going to have this break now, then they won't have it hanging over them, the anxiety.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: My Lord, yes.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: Thank you very much indeed.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Is that all right, Mr Johnson?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes. We timetabled Professor Arthurs for the 21st, but he had offered, I think, the day before if necessary and he said he could re-arrange things to accommodate that so I'm just trying to give him as much notice as possible.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: That's helpful. Thank you very much.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: (In the presence of the jury)
Good morning, members of the jury. I've received some notes about requests not to sit on certain days, which I have just been discussing with counsel.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: To put the minds of those who are asking for the days off at rest, I agree to not sitting on the days requested, so we will not be sitting on 21 April, we will not be sitting on the 22nd, the 23rd and 26 May either.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: What I'm going to do is put all these dates on a list for you and give it to you before we part company this afternoon so you have an up-to-date list of days when we will not be sitting. I just wanted those of you who made the requests to know that they will be accommodated. All right? Thank you very much.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes, Mr Johnson.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: DR SANDIE BOHIN (recalled)
Examination-in-chief by MR JOHNSON
My Lord, I recall Dr Bohin, please, who is already in the witness box.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Just for the sake of the record, please, would you confirm your identity?
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: I'm Dr Sandie Bohin.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: Thank you. Dr Bohin, concerning the case of [Baby Q], have you signed four separate reports/statements?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: Is the first and compendious report 16 April 2019?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: Subsequently, have you signed statements dated 10 June 2021, 5 October 2021 and 15 October 2021?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: Albeit those of June and 15 October 2021 deal essentially with pagination issues rather than the essence of your evidence?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: The 15 October one is not a pagination one, the previous two are. 15 October was a statement in relation to direct questions asked of me.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: Sorry, yes. I'm reversing the 5th and 15 October, I think. Thank you for correcting me.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Can we just start, as always, by confirming the material that you received. It's paragraph 4.3 of your report of 16 April. Did you receive the notes from the Countess of Chester Hospital together with X-rays?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: Material from Alder Hey, being medical and pathological records?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: Probably most of that material was in a binder of material which consisted of 816 pages?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: That's correct.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: And did you also receive two witness statements made by Dr Evans, dated 3 June 2018 and 25 January 2019?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: Was your approach to [Baby Q]'s case essentially the same as your approach to the other 16 cases that you have already given evidence about?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, it was.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: Just dealing with the chronology and taking it up from your section 6 of your report, did you record the time and circumstances and date of [Baby Q]'s birth on 22 June?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: Did you address in general terms the issues of his ventilation and how that was managed?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: The fact that he was taken off CPAP on 23 June 2016 at 11.30 hours?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: Did you, at your paragraph 6.7, record the fact that he remained well, his abdomen was not distended, he was passing meconium, a fact that we have noted at 18.00 hours on 23 June in the hard copy documents at page 24311?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: Which is page 3B in section 22 of the hard copy documents that the jury have.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Moving on to 24 June, which of course is the day before the event with which we are primarily concerned, did you record the fact that [Baby Q] was started on milk feeds of a half of one millilitre every 2 hours?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: Did you note the aspirations that had been recorded in the records?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: At your paragraph 6.9, which is our tile 70, did you summarise the essence of the nursing note that [Baby Q]'s abdomen was full but soft?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: And that his blood gases were "not as good"?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: Did you note in particular that prior to 09.10 hours -so I'm now looking at your paragraph 6.10 -- on 25 June the records suggest that [Baby Q]'s abdomen was not distended?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: That's correct.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: And in this respect can we just go to, with Mr Murphy's assistance, tile 102, please. It's the top left-hand corner of the page, please, Mr Murphy.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: This is Lucy Letby's note for the day shift. If you could expand that section.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: This is a note written between 12.53 and 13.04:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Written for care given from 08.00 to present. Emergency equipment checked, fluids calculated, [Baby Q] nursed in an incubator."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Et cetera, et cetera. Then we see just at the end of that first section it says:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Abdomen soft and non-distended."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: And the note then moves on to the events of 09.10 hours. Is that what you were referring to at your paragraph 6.10?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: Thank you. Keeping that on the screen if we may, please, Mr Murphy. At your paragraph 6.11, did you summarise the essence of Lucy Letby's note that appears in the bottom half of the screen as we are now looking at it?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: Did you refer to the fact that there had been suction of the oro- and nasopharynx, that that had been said to yield "clear fluid +++", which is probably a reference to Minna Lappalainen's note at the previous tile, 102?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: That [Baby Q] had been bagged with the Neopuff, given oxygen, the NGT had been aspirated and that that had yielded "air ++", as we see recorded there by --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: -- Lucy Letby? Did you then refer to observation charts?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, I did.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: It may be easier in this respect to go to divider 22 of the hard copy documents that we have. It's difficult to read the pagination that's been put on the top right-hand corner because it's partly obliterated by the NHS logo, but it's the second page, page 2, bottom right-hand corner, page J24307.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: We see that this is an observation chart which begins at 08.30 hours on 24 June; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: So by a necessary inference, the events of the 25th, albeit not marked with a date, begin about eight columns in from the right-hand side of the page at 03.00 hours?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: Actually, 24.30 would have been 25/06, so nine columns in.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: And you refer there to [Baby Q]'s heart rate and respiratory rate; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes. In my statement I'd written that the heart rate gradually increased to around 200. Actually, that's a mistake on my part. At that time the heart rate was around 165, but the heart rate had increased.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: Yes. I think the increase up to about 200 is on the next page.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: That's about 20.00 hours, the same day, on the 25th --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: -- where they're marked in manuscript at 198.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: Did you refer also to the venous blood gas taken after [Baby Q]'s desaturation at 09.10?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: That's at tile 118, but it's also in the hard copy documents on page 8 or 24326 of section 22 in that file.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Dealing with events concerning what happened at about 09.10 hours, at your paragraph 6.13 did you record the fact that medical staff were called urgently to [Baby Q]?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: That by the time they arrived, he'd been bagged and his saturations were 100%?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: His partial septic screen was carried out and his antibiotics changed to teicoplanin and cefotaxime?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: That he was given a bolus of intravenous saline and his nasogastric tube was put on to free drainage and that series of events subsequently improved his perfusion?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: Again, the notes describe [Baby Q]'s abdomen as not distended?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: At a later stage, 3ml of milk/mucus were aspirated from the nasogastric tube, and [Baby Q] was put back on to CPAP; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: Actually, the gas chart that we have on the screen there is quite a good ready reckoner, isn't it, for when [Baby Q] was or wasn't on CPAP?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: So just summarising that position, we see that from his birth, at the top of the gas chart there -- he'd been born a couple of hours earlier -- SIMV; what does that mean, please?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Synchronous intermittent mandatory ventilation. So that's -- he was put on to invasive ventilation using a breathing tube. That's a form of ventilation.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: Yes. Then on to CPAP at 16.57, which continued --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: -- until some time between 00.55 and 13.27 on the 23rd, when he was self-ventilating in air; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: Then we see that position continued past the time at which he desaturated at 09.10?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: Then back on to CPAP?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: Over the page on to page 9, we see the ventilator again, SIMV, at the top there?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: That's correct.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: That's the position that continued so far as that chart is concerned?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, until he got transferred.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: Thank you. You refer to the fact that, following [Baby Q]'s collapse at 09.10, the results of the septic screen, when they came back, were unremarkable; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes. The omission there is the platelet count had fallen to 95 from 196 but the rest of the septic screen was unremarkable.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: You refer to, albeit he had a good blood gas at 11.12 hours -- and that's the third line up from the bottom of page 8 in the hard copy, J24326 -- he was later described as being tired with a falling respiratory rate and increasing heart rate, which we saw on the second page of the observation charts?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, that's correct.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: That, of course, was referred to yesterday by [Dr A].
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: There were minimal aspirates following that, but as the day progressed into the evening, he developed an oxygen requirement and was therefore electively intubated and ventilated. As we heard yesterday from [Dr A], that was at 19.20 hours on the 25th, which is our tile 197.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: Following that, overnight, the 25th into the 26th, you recount the medical attention that he received and I think part of that was referred to by Dr Gibbs yesterday.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: You move on at your paragraph 6.17 to refer to the examination of [Baby Q] on the morning of Sunday, 26 June at 08.56?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: And the fact that [Dr A] was able to feel a loop in the right upper quadrant, about which he told us yesterday?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: That's correct.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: That an abdominal X-ray was then taken?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: And that also is the X-ray that was shown to us yesterday, taken shortly before midday?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: That's right, although in my note I've written that the dilated loop is in the upper right upper quadrant and in fact the X-ray shows the dilated loop is in the left upper quadrant.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: Yes, thank you. That precipitated the suspicion of NEC and that the antibiotic metronidazole was added to his drug regime?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: That's correct.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: Following that, at your paragraph 6.18, do you record the fact that a referral was made to the surgical team at Alder Hey and he was subsequently transferred?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: How did you summarise the position once [Baby Q] had been transferred?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: He settled very quickly once he'd been transferred to Alder Hey. There was no further vomiting. The aspirates from his nasogastric tube were not excessive.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: There was no further bile that I could see from the aspirates. And he was eventually extubated fairly shortly, a day or so after arriving -- the next day in fact, after arriving at Alder Hey. The abdominal X-rays that they took were reported as showing no evidence of necrotising enterocolitis.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: The other condition that had been questioned was whether [Baby Q] had what a volvulus. That's a condition where the bowel sort of twists on itself because that can cause that sort of X-ray appearance, but it was clear to the team at Alder Hey that he didn't have that either. And there was no sign of any perforation. So they, I think, were very cautious in that they felt that he should continue to be treated for possible necrotising enterocolitis, although that wasn't confirmed. But he was repatriated to the Countess of Chester on the 28th.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: Yes. So Dr Bohin, can we move on to section 7, please, and deal with your observations and opinion. Can you talk us through your review, please?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Well, yes, initially [Baby Q] was obviously a baby who was premature and needed some respiratory support very soon after birth, but within a short space of time he was taken off the ventilator and on to CPAP and remained well.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: The team at Chester decided that they would feed him and normally when a baby's at this gestation, when you feed, you give very small volumes of feed; I think it's been referred to already as trophic feeds. And that's a way of getting the gut used to accepting more substantial volumes of feed. So it's a way of priming the gut.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: Babies don't always absorb those feeds but it's a way of giving small amounts and to try and get the gut working. The team in Chester decided they would do that for [Baby Q], but actually rather than giving small amounts, the first two feeds that he had were 2ml an hour rather than 0.5ml on alternate hours. And he -- when the nurses aspirated the tube, they actually found some bile -- it says "light bile aspirates".
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: Now, bile can be very light, very light green or can be very dark green, and there is a kind of grading of this. So "light bile aspirate" I think I would note and I would watch, but I wouldn't pay too much attention to it.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: Later on, at 21.30 that day, early on, the nurse looking after him has recorded that she'd aspirated 2ml of -- in the notes it says blood and bile, but when she gave evidence she said it was coffee grounds. Now, coffee grounds are altered blood and they are like you would see coffee grounds, they are dark brown. So if bile is mixed in with dark brown, I'm not quite sure how you would see that.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: Clearly, blood, if it's red mixed with bile, would be very obvious to see, but in her evidence she said it was coffee grounds. So I'm not sure whether this was fresh or old blood that she aspirated. But regardless, the staff took that seriously and stopped any further feeds that day and they were not restarted until a day or so later, when they were started at half a millilitre alternate hours. And the staff were continuing to aspirate that tube and there was no more blood for the duration of [Baby Q]'s stay at the Countess of Chester, so no more blood was aspirated up that tube.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: From there on, [Baby Q], on the 24th, was fed alternate hours. There were some aspirates, but I think they were not excessive in the scheme of things. It's not uncommon for babies to have some feed intolerance and I think that's probably what [Baby Q] had.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: On the 24th there was no bile seen at all on that day and the feeds were returned -- the aspirates that they got were returned with the feed. But throughout this time, the abdomen was either described as being normal or full but soft.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: Up until the time [Baby Q] deteriorated, the day prior to that he was given feeds at 3 o'clock, 5 o'clock and 7 o'clock in the morning. And then no other recording is made of milk administration that day.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: I'm sorry --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Have I gone on too far?
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: I'm going to ask, just so we can follow what you're describing, Mr Murphy to put up tile 62, please.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: It does make it easier.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: That's at page 11 in the hard copy because we're at the critical time in effect. So just so we can assimilate what you're describing with what is recorded.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: This is the fluid balance chart which, as we can see from the left-hand -- under where it says "date", it says "25 June".
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Somebody has written in manuscript, underneath the time 01.00, "01.30".
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: We see that Babiven was being given via the UVC as the main source of nutrition.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: There were lipids as well in the second block of rows.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: And further down, under two more fluid blocks, we have:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Feeds. NGT/OGT. Bottle/breast. Please circle."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Which nobody has.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: We see then that the reference to half of 1ml of expressed breast milk being given to [Baby Q] -- I think you said 3.00, 5.00 and 7.00 hours; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: We see the corresponding aspirates under the output rows right at the bottom of the page, as Mr Murphy has now --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: -- highlighted. So with that data in mind, can you just run through that part of your explanation again, please?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes. So feeds were given, as they had been before, at 0.5ml and at 3 o'clock 3ml of nasogastric aspirate had been obtained; the R denotes that that was returned.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: At 5 o'clock, ordinarily there would have been a feed but there wasn't and I'm not sure of the reason for that.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: I think there is at 5 in the feeds --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I beg your pardon. I mean there's no aspirates, sorry.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: The feed is given but there's no mention of any aspirate, that's left blank. So I don't know if it wasn't aspirated or whether nothing was obtained. But at 7 o'clock, a further 1.5ml of aspirate was obtained and that was returned.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: The next feed would be due at 9 o'clock and obviously there's nothing in that column.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: Yes. If Mr Murphy wouldn't mind zooming out so we can see the full -- it's not brilliantly clear on the screen because of the size. Thank you.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: So we see just by where there's a black --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: -- round object, which is clearly or might be thought to be a photocopy artefact from where there would be a hole in the page where somebody's put it into a file, we see what may be the initials LL under the 8 o'clock column.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: We see that LL has recorded the fluids going in as Babiven --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: -- and the lipids.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: There's then some ticks in the third block. Can you decipher what's written there or what that means for us?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: (Pause). At the far left, it says "zeroed later". So that relates to something at 1 o'clock. Then I can't see what...
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I can't -- oh.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: Something warm?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Something warm.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: Pink and warm, is it?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, pink and warm. But that's in the fluid column.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: That doesn't actually make any sense. I think it's, "Pink [tick], warm [tick]".
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: All right.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I don't think that helps with regard to the fluids.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: No, it's just in case anyone asked what it was, I thought we might as well deal with it with you if you could help. The words appear in the 7 o'clock column, the ticks appear in the 8 o'clock column.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

The whole issue around the treatment of possible NEC is fraught with difficulty and making a diagnosis is, as I say, based on Xray findings and surgical findings. Prior to that, you'd have to say this is a presumptive diagnosis and I don't think there's enough here to give a presumptive diagnosis of NEC.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: I'm not talking about a diagnosis, I'm talking about the fact it's consistent with early stage NEC, isn't it?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: It's consistent with early stage NEC.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: And in fact the abdominal -- the loops or the loop felt by [Dr A] when he was palpating [Baby Q]'s stomach is something that could be consistent with that, isn't it?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: It could be consistent with an ileus as well, which is not related to any underlying pathology.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: And the abdominal X-ray that was taken, again, is consistent with NEC, isn't it?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, it's also consistent with a volvulus, it's also consistent with an ileus, which a -- a volvulus is very, very serious. An ileus is not, it just means that your tummy isn't working the same -- as anyone who has had abdominal surgery will realise, their tummy doesn't work for a while after they've had surgery, so it's also consistent with that, but it's not pathognomonic of NEC.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: No. We're looking at what could be here.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Could we go to page 24200, please, 24200 at the end of this section. 24200, I apologise. Where we've got impression, Dr Bohin:
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: "Probable NEC, Bell's stage 2."
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: That is an impression that is utterly reasonable on the circumstances that [Dr A] was dealing with, isn't it?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: He says "probable NEC", I'd say "possible NEC", but it's absolutely reasonable for him to have carried out the actions that he did, yes.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: Then if it is treated in the appropriate way, which may be conservative, that can succeed in resolving that problem, can't it?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: It can, but I would say that [Baby Q], I think, got better too quickly for that to be the case. So children that have mild NEC, the treatment is to give gut rest, so you don't feed them, usually for around 10 days, and to give three antibiotics empirically. And you rest their gut for 10 days before very slowly reintroducing feeds.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: Now here he did have conservative treatment, but also he recovered, got off the ventilator, didn't have any more bilious
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: aspirates, didn't have any bloody aspirates, didn't have any bloody stools. His gut was completely fine within 24 hours and he was off the ventilator, so for me that isn't a baby that's got mild NEC.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: If he had, as you put it, bloody aspirates and bilious aspirates and the things we've seen, there was something wrong with him, wasn't there?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I think he had an ileus. He didn't have bloody aspirates. That was days and days before. That was several days before. I don't think that had anything to do with his collapse and I don't think that had anything to do with what happened after he was ventilated.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: I think he had an ileus because he had been destabilised, he was on very large doses of morphine, which would account for what was seen once he was ventilated. I don't think he had NEC -well, he didn't have NEC. You know, the Alder Hey surgeons sent him back as he didn't have NEC.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: Well, that's as conjectural as saying you can make a diagnosis of NEC, Dr Bohin. He may have had it, he may have been treated conservatively, he may have recovered and come back. That's entirely possible, isn't it?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: If that's the case, he got better remarkably quickly for a baby with the early stages of NEC.
blocks.speaker: BOHIN

blocks.text: Thank you, Dr Bohin.

blocks.text: "No worries. Can have a proper chat as not had the chance."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Were there then some following messages about work but not about a specific baby?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes. Lucy Letby replied to [Nurse E]:
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "Thank you."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: [Dr A] then said:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Lucy, you did nothing wrong at all. It's an odd time to ring but you've had a rough few days and a good manager would realise that."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Lucy Letby replied to [Nurse E]:
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "It's late, isn't it?"
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "Yeah, very."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Wish she'd done this earlier because I'd have just gone in and spoken to her."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "Yeah, not been given an opportunity and naughty to leave till tomoz."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Messes with your head a bit to be told that at this time. Would have sounded more reasonable if had done it earlier, which is why I wonder if it is coming from higher up as she usually finishes at 4.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "Anyway, we'll chat later."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "Yeah. Try not to worry too much."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Then [Dr A]:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "There is no problem. I suspect my head is in about the same place. The management was appropriate and your recognition of an unwell baby was spot on. The care delivered was quick and accurate. I can't fault anything with your delivery of care to
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: either baby last week. If there was anything, I would have said so. Eirian knows you. Has there ever been a reason for you not to trust her?"
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Lucy Letby replied:
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "I can't talk about this now."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "Okay."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Sorry, I just need a bit of time."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Then 12 minutes later she sent a further message?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Sorry, that was rude. Felt completely overwhelmed and panicked for a minute. We all worked tirelessly and did everything possible. I don't see how anyone can question that. E has always been very supportive."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: [Dr A]:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "No, it wasn't rude. It was unexpected and that's never nice. Okay now?"
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "I'm having a meltdown ++ but think that's what I need to do.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "Anyway, I'll be okay. You have enough on your plate too."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: [Dr A]:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "When I said it was unexpected, I meant the phone call.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Maybe a meltdown will help. You said your head is a mess. This could be the way to clear things."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Then [Nurse E] responded:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "At the end of the day there's been no common factors in any of it and a lot of other people involved."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Lucy Letby replied to [Nurse E]:
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "I know. I think everyone worked tirelessly and don't see how any of that could be questioned. I imagine she may want to know why I had triplets back the next day and why I had [Baby Q] sat but there are reasons for that and wouldn't have prevented me from being part on resus."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: That's to [Nurse E] and this next one is from [Dr A]:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "There isn't anything to question. You've already done what anybody with neonatal knowledge would do: look at the situation, look [at] the intervention and look at the response. You didn't give any drugs that hasn't been checked or made by anyone else. You didn't delay any treatment and your suggestions were all perfectly appropriate. There is nothing that could have been done differently."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Followed up by:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "E was a good manager when I was here last time. There isn't a high staff turnover, which suggests the unit is well run. She is most likely going to do what [Dr B] did with me last night and go through it too [it should be probably 'to'] check you're okay. There is nothing to be gained by not addressing how your staff have bene hit by an event. You didn't look well Sat. Maybe that was noticed."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Lucy Letby replied to [Dr A]:
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "No, you are right. I think she will maybe question why I had [Babies P & R] on Fri but there were reasons for that and even if I hadn't been looking after them, I would still have been involved with the resus, drugs, etc. Same as there is a reason I had to keep [Baby Q] on Sat. It's just hit me a bit as was an unexpected call. If she had phoned earlier I wouldn't have worried."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "Yeah".
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I think that's an incoming from [Nurse E].
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Sorry, yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Lucy Letby replies to [Nurse E]:
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "Perhaps she waited so long to ring as was waiting to see if could find cover."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: [Nurse E] responded:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "If was that bothered, could always work herself!"
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "That's true!"
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Is the next one an SMS message that's on the phone but was never actually sent to anyone?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: So it's almost like a note on a phone but in the text part of the phone?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes:
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "Death Datix x2. Datix. No bicarb delay in IO access. Sign out FFP on Meditech and pink chart. J charts obs. Fluids in sluice. Sign drugs. Sign Curosurf out. Traffic light drug compatibility. Inotropes and no policy for panc. Delay in people doing drugs."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday were days back at work for Lucy Letby, doing a long day shift; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: And after the long day shift on 30 June, Thursday the 30th, [Dr A] sent a message to her saying:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Did J tell you what was wrong earlier?"
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Lucy Letby replied:
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "Not really. We started talking but then people came into nursery and she dashed off."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Then we come to messages that were -- about which [Dr A] was asked yesterday, so I'll deal with these slightly more slowly. At 23.55, [Dr A] to Lucy Letby:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "I'm not sure where the information has come from. It seems that on the SHO grapevine somebody at Liverpool Women's Hospital has said that one of the triplets was found to have a ruptured liver. J was upset that this may have been caused by her chest compressions."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Lucy Letby replied:
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "Oh no, that's awful.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "No wonder she's upset. Were you able to reassure her?
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Then 4 minutes later, but over into Friday, 1 July, [Dr A] responds:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "We spent 20 minutes in a cubicle going over everything. The CPR was all at the 5th rib space, between the nipples. The DuoDERM on [Baby P] was high. If there was anything, it will have been due to fluid volume causing liver distension."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Then:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "I'm not sure I believe it.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "It was a coroner's PM. It usually takes weeks to get any report."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Lucy Letby replied:
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "It seems a bit like a rumour mill has gone into overdrive. The boys were only returned today. Can't see how info would be out that quick."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "No, me neither."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Not nice for J though. Can see how it would play on her mind."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "This has come at the end of a seven-day run for her, not a good time."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "No. It's good that she felt able to tell you."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "I'm good for a hug and a chat. I think I helped."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "She said she'd spoken and cried on you and Huw and was feeling better for it."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: That day, Friday 1 July, was a day off for Lucy Letby, as was the following day, Saturday the 2nd and Sunday the 3rd.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Monday the 4th and Tuesday the 5th were annual leave days and we come next to a message sent at 14.16 on Tuesday the 5th by [Nurse E] to Lucy Letby:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "I only found out yest about the business with J's UVC."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Lucy Letby replied:
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "Really? I thought they were going to take it straight out. Did he still have it in?"
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "Yes."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Then she says:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "[Dr A] came in chatting to me at the start of last night's shift and said A needs L.L soon as UVC been in nearly 2 weeks and he said something about J's already being changed and I said it hadn't and he told me about the open port."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Lucy Letby replied to [Nurse E]:
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "Jeez, well, that was on Thursday. [Dr A] didn't have time to look for access in the evening so had to label it and not use port overnight and they would sort it the next day. Abby new."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: From [Nurse E]:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "I handed over to Abby this morning and she said she knew nothing about it being changed and why would it be."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: And Lucy Letby replied:
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "Bloody hell. Thank goodness I did a Datix."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "Did you? Good.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Well, when that gets looked into they'll see it never got changed."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Lucy Letby replied:
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "I told her about it that night. Yes, because thought it's a massive infection risk and risk of air embolism. Don't know how long it had been like that."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Then two messages from [Nurse E] in very quick succession:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "He has been persistently tachycardic now and tachypnoeic. Feeds slow to increase as having few vomits, larger aspirates so asked for a review last night.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Jess and Tony not bothered as CRP less than 1 on weekly bloods."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: And was there then a continuing conversation regarding a UVC?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: (No audible answer).
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Moving on to Wednesday, 6 July, shortly after midnight, [Dr A] sent a series of messages to Lucy Letby, starting at 00.54:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "You need to keep this to yourself: the meeting this afternoon looked at everything with [Babies O & P] from birth onwards.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "We reviewed everything: room, meds, medical reviews and actions. We looked at all documentation, MED and NUR.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "If you've any doubt about how good you are at your job, stop now.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Documentation was perfect. Everything commented about the appropriateness of your request for a review of [Baby O] following vomit.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Your documentation of the resus/incubation [it maybe should be intubation] drugs was faultless. There is absolutely nothing for you to worry about. Please don't.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "There are going to be some recommendations based on staffing/kit but there was no criticism of either resus.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "This is staying quiet until has been to execs. We're looking at [Baby R] care on Thur."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Then the final message in this sequence is at 01.06:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "E had nothing but good things to say about you."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Lucy Letby replied at 01.14:
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "Okay. I really appreciate you telling me. It won't go any further. I was one member of a huge team effort, but you know I've been carrying the worry of the 'what if I wasn't enough'. It's reassuring to hear that it doesn't appear that anything could have been done differently or that I didn't act on or do something I should have. Thank you."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "I was invited to attend because SB and [redacted] [that may be Stephen Brearey] thought it was good consultant preparation for me. I gave extra details of both resus as they were required.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "There were a few questions which were easy to answer but the constant theme was how well you and I dealt with [Baby O] deterioration and with [Baby P] resus. I felt proud for both of us."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Lucy Letby replied:
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "That's good to hear. I'm glad you've had positive feedback too. You were fantastic. It was an awful situation but I wouldn't have wanted anyone else to be there. I now feel confident that we did absolutely everything and it's reassuring to know that the documentation reflects that."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "There was a liver capsule haemorrhage in [Baby O]. It is thought to be related to resus/disease process but doesn't explain the deterioration (not on first X-ray). It's not considered by SB and [redacted] to be significant.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "There will be an inquest, we may have to attend."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Would he have died from that?"
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "I don't think so. He collapsed. The liver on first Xray looked normal (done in nursery 2) and looked abnormal on second X-ray to confirm tube position. But the CPR was needed for something. It doesn't explain why liver changed appearance."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Okay."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "Thank you. I wouldn't have wanted anyone else but you to be looking after [Baby O] or [Baby P]. We do work well together!"
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Then:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "[Baby Q] care is going to be reviewed on Thur as well because of acute deterioration."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "That makes sense."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "They're looking at me because I was involved in all."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Have they said that?"
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "Not in so many words. I document clearly and contemporaneously. It's difficult to pull my work apart but there were a couple of comments, which is fine as long as I get the chance to talk through the process."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Okay. I imagine they will look at us both (as E has done with me for previous babies). If there are any concerns
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: they will have to give you the opportunity to discuss it. I don't envisage anything being a major problem if they've gone through both today and nothing was said.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "And you weren't the only doctor involved."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "I ran [Babies O & P] and was the only doctor involved with [Baby Q]."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "But [Dr B] was present at all times. [Baby Q] was different but you kept JG updated.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "Try not to worry about it unless anything is said. They will be covering all areas."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "I know, I'm not worried."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Good. Thank you for telling me."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "I thought you ought to know. I was so sorry that you were upset when E called about that night when I knew you'd done a perfect job.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Just had the email."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "I took it the wrong way, but it completely floored me. Was overwhelmed by it all.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "Eek!"
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "I think 'eek' sums it up perfectly."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Scary but exciting."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: And sends an emoji with an emoji going back the other way. And a further one from Lucy Letby to [Dr A].
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Everything happens for a reason. It'll all work out. This is the start of a new beginning."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Then that day, Wednesday the 6th, was Lucy Letby on annual leave and did the messaging resume just before midnight, at 23.13, with one from [Dr A]:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "As far as meetings go, I've plumbed new depths today. Big relief. I managed to hand it back without upsetting anybody"?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Lucy Letby replied:
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "How come? You've escaped and everyone is happy. Result!"
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: [Dr A]:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "The ceilidh is a good result. PTA meeting was just tedious. [Dr B] came to NNU in a bit of a flap between my LLs. She's going on holiday tomorrow and wanted to go through the notes to make a formal timeline. She was a bit fixated on the IO needles. I think the fact that you got a needlestick is making them question if it was displaced during the resus. She took an age. I had to tell her that I needed to go and pick T up. I've since had an email from SB which makes me understand what is going on. Will forward it to you. You might find it interesting."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Lucy Letby replied:
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "Ah, okay. It hadn't penetrated the skin when I gave him to parents, etc, but not to say it hadn't dislodged. It was used for the last few drugs in the final round. Oh yes, send it me."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "Which email address (secure one) should I send it to?"
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "lletby@nhs.net."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Is there then an email sent which reads as follows -so [Dr A] copying Lucy Letby or forwarding to Lucy Letby an email sent from Dr Brearey on 7 July or the date on it --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: It's 6 July.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Sorry. On that it says the 7th on the screen, doesn't it? If you look on the screen, sorry.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes. I think that's an error.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: That should read the 6th on the screen, should it?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes --
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Okay.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes. Anyway, it reads:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Hi [Dr A]. Having thought about the two cases we discussed yesterday, I think it is quite likely both will go to inquest and you are likely to be asked to give a statement. Can I suggest you prepare it now when everything is fresh in your mind? It can include things we discussed yesterday that might not be in the notes, particularly around [Baby P]'s initial arrest and who put IOs in and where and what went through them.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "If you need any help with the format, etc, please let me know. I have suggested the same to [Dr B] and will ask Huw and Tony to do the same. [Dr B] has the notes for both babies at the moment but I think is away on leave at the end of the week. If you do use the notes for reference after [Dr B], can I ask you don't take them off the hospital and don't keep them for too long. If you need to use any of the consultant offices, including mine, feel free. For your information also, I thought your record keeping was clearer and more comprehensive than everyone else's. Steve."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: And [Dr A] sent a message saying:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Okay, I've just sent it."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Oh, okay.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "How do feel about it?"
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: I think "you" is supposed to be in the original message.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "A bit upset.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "I've had a coroner's PM before which found a clear anatomical cause. The inquest was cancelled and after a serious case review in which everything was okay, it was put to rest.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "This is different. The meeting yesterday found no issue with management or drugs, etc, but doing this in a court is going to be uncomfortable."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Why is it going to inquest?"
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "Unexplained cause x2."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "It's a bit of a worry if it's going that far. Do you think I'll be involved?"
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "Probably not. Your documentation will most likely be used in place of a statement. The questions will be about management and procedures."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "I don't know what to say. Feels like a bit of a blow considering everyone's hard work, etc."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "I feel the same. Statement writing is a peculiar art form. Takes ages getting everything to flow properly.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "(Or maybe that's just me)."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "I imagine it's a lot of work.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "Accuracy of events, times, etc.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "Huw wasn't there, was he?"
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "I'd ignore that bit."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Okay."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "I know you won't say anything. This email has to stay between us. Is that okay?"
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Of course, 100%."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "It's going to take a day to write each of the reports.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: They may never be asked for but I think they will be asked for in August."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Worth doing ASAP and then you've got them."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Did Lucy Letby then have 8 days off between Thursday the 7th and Thursday, 14 July?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: I say off. The final day was a management day, I think; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Followed by a day off on Friday, 15 July.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Was there then an email from Yvonne Griffiths to all the nurses at the Countess of Chester Hospital, sent on Friday, 15 July at 11.16?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Reading as follows:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Hi everyone. In preparation for the external review it has been decided that all members of staff need to undertake a period of clinical supervision. Due to our staffing issues, it has been difficult to determine how we undertake this process. We can only support one member of staff at a time, therefore we have decided that it would be useful to commence with staff who have been involved in many of the acute events, facilitating a supportive role to each individual. Therefore Lucy has agreed to undergo this supervision first, commencing on Monday, 18 July 2016. I appreciate that this process may be an added stress factor in an already emotive environment, but we need to ensure that we can assure a safe environment, in addition to safeguarding not only our babies but our staff. This is not meant to be a blame or a competency issue, but a way forward to ensure that our practice is safe. It will probably be developed into a competence-based programme to be undertaken every 2 to 3 years in line with our mandatory update training. Kindest regards, Eirian."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: And then Eirian Lloyd-Powell's details are set out underneath.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Was that followed 4.5 hours later by a message sent by Lucy Letby to [Nurse E]?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "I've done a timeline of this year."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "Fab.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "And how quite a few babies weren't compatible with life anyway.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "I wonder if midwives get this amount of stillbirths?"
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Yes, and some went off within hours/on handover."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "Yep."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Or were already acutely unwell when I took over."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "Exactly."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "I put that when [Baby Q] went off no other staff able to care for him, etc."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "Not like all behaving fantastically til right into shift.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Yeah."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Hoping to get as much info together as possible. If they have nothing or minimal on me, they'll look silly, not me."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL
